verdict: APPROVED. E1 is resolved and this is an E1-only delta. A new session_signals module installs checked sigaction dispositions before any session file, listener, device or process work: SIGPIPE=SIG_IGN; SIGCHLD=SIG_DFL with flags 0, clearing inherited SIG_IGN/SA_NOCLDWAIT auto-reap; INT/TERM/HUP get the stop handler with SA_RESTART. Each install saves the full old action. On setup failure it rolls back. After run_session's cleanup and drops, it restores in reverse and attempts every restore even after an earlier error. A restore failure is a nonzero session failure even if the inner result was already sealed, and it poisons later entries. Source and host evidence only.

binding.replay: verify_checkpoint.py (temp dir in scratch): 'Verified003 cumulative 23 and incremental 3 files, full tree and dependencies'. The 002 receipt recomputes as 257b9e77 (unchanged).
binding.delta: There are exactly three incremental files. desktop_entry.rs: run() now calls with_process_signals(&STOP, stop, || run_session(options)), and the 002 STOP.store and libc::signal loop are removed. lib.rs: a private mod session_signals. session_signals.rs is new (366 lines including tests). All non-delta bytes equal 002.

checks.action_construction: new_action zeroes the struct, sets sa_sigaction to the handler (SIG_IGN, SIG_DFL or the stop function), uses sa_flags 0 for PIPE and CHLD and SA_RESTART only for INT/TERM/HUP, and empties sa_mask with a checked sigemptyset (session_signals.rs:18-34).
checks.xnu_autoreap: In the pinned XNU kern_sig.c:675-685, a SIGCHLD sigaction sets P_NOCLDWAIT only for SA_NOCLDWAIT or SIG_IGN, and otherwise clears it (P_NOCLDSTOP likewise). So SIG_DFL with flags 0 really clears inherited auto-reap, and the manager's exclusive waitpid cannot be turned into ECHILD 'ownership lost' by an inherited disposition.
checks.order_and_scope: The order is PIPE, CHLD, INT, TERM, HUP, all before run_session opens records, socket, fonts, devices or the manager. 002 installed the stop handlers only after the listener bind. STOP is reset under the entry claim. The calling thread's blocked-signal mask is deliberately left unchanged (documented).
checks.restoration: restore_all pops saved actions in reverse and attempts each one even after an earlier error, recording every errno with no retry. checked_scope wraps the body in an outer catch_unwind, so a panic outside the inner frame coordinator (for example in seal) still restores dispositions; the panic is reported, never turned into app-cleanup success. A value is returned only for Ok(Ok) with no restore errors; otherwise Failure carries setup, restore, body and panicked. A setup failure at any of the 5 positions rolls back the saved prefix and never runs the body.
checks.reentry_and_poison: EntryClaim uses compare_exchange on ACTIVE to refuse a concurrent or nested managed entry and releases on drop. POISONED is set when any restore fails, and every later entry in the process is refused. Unrelated process-global sigaction users are explicitly not synchronized (documented single-process scope).
checks.exit_semantics: with_process_signals maps any Failure to Err, so desktop_main prints and exits 1. A qualifying run therefore needs actual executable exit 0 after restoration, not just a sealed session-result.txt. That matches the frozen qualification_contract postseal_failure clause.

notes.S1_sigpipe_context: Informational correction to my 002 E1 note. Rust std normally sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN before main on unix (not verified here against the pinned toolchain's source, because no rust-src is present). The substantive E1 gain is therefore the SIGCHLD auto-reap clearing plus explicit, checked, restorable dispositions. The C shim still resets SIGPIPE to default in spawned children through its setsigdefault set.
